It is April 17, 2026 now. My wheat is already standing in the field, so this year my main job is to carry the wheat through to harvest, then turn that land quickly into summer maize, and at the same time manage the vegetable plots carefully because vegetables bring cash but also cost more money and labor.

I’m 68 now, so I don’t want to spread myself too thin. I have only 7.5 mu, and with five people in the house I can still rely on family labor, but I cannot gamble too much on expensive inputs. The extension guy said vegetables can make more money, but they also eat fertilizer, water, and pesticide. So I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on the main land because it is steady, and I will keep some cabbage, chili, and eggplant for cash income. For fertilizer, I still do it the practical way: enough so the crop does not look weak, but not so much that I tie up all my cash at the start. Wheat I will finish with one more topdress if the stand still looks hungry. After wheat harvest, maize must go in fast, within a few days, otherwise I lose summer moisture. For vegetables, I will spend more attention because if I manage water and pests poorly, the whole plot can go backwards very quickly.
